answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the direct evience that the low-cost vendor can serve as primary supplier (sharp unit-cost cut, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing). memory_c1 is the counter-evience to weigh: it shows that renewing with the incumbent preserved integration stability and uninterrupted deliveries across two cycles. I need to check whether c1's stability concerns apply to a full switch (not just a renewal) and whether c2's track record is sufficient to absorb the delivery risk given the assembly line is at 94% with no buffer. If both archives support the read that the low-cost vendor's onboarding was genuinely smooth and the incumbent-renewal benefit was primarily about avoiding migration work (which c2 suggests is minimal), then switching primary vendor meets the 18% mandate alone at lowest TCO without adding a second sourcing action this cycle. The remaining capacity constraint and the 14-day deadline make any other direction either too slow (add_second_source) or insufficient (renew_incumbent alone does not meet the cut). Deferring is ruled out by the hard expiry; negotiating terms is subordinate to the switch decision and can follow next cycle.
